task: compose and send an email in a mail client (Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo Mail, Apple Mail): open compose, address the recipient, write the subject and body, optionally attach a file, send it, and verify it in Sent; complete when the message shows as sent. Surface pinned: the mail client's compose-and-send flow — not inbox-organizing tours, not newsletter/marketing tools, not email-etiquette advice videos.

tree.label: Send an email
tree.note: 1 when the client is not already open and signed in - most keepers start authenticated and skip most of it. then 2: a new message, or a reply or forward entered from 8.1 (DFXu, ycKB, 6rzA, 0D7H, zCsj), which decides how much of 3 is left to do. 3 and 4 in either order - HnFK writes the subject and body before the recipient. 5 where the message carries a file; 5.4 only when the client refuses the file, and it returns into 5.2 or 5.5 once the file is ready (UehN never gets back). then 6, one of 6.2 to 6.5; 6.6 and 6.7 where the client interrupts. then 7 - in this corpus that's where the task actually completes, and 7 is skipped by seven keepers. 8 at any point.

questions.question: What information should you enter into the recipient, subject, and body fields?
questions.why: The New Message screen contains blank fields that must be filled with the correct contact and message content to ensure the email reaches the right person and conveys your intent.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose control over the exact wording, tone, and specific recipient of your communication.

children.label: Get into the mailbox
children.note: 1.1 then 1.2. 1.3 only from a logged-out start - two keepers. 1.4 where more than one account is signed in. 1.5 and 1.6 as orientation before any composing, and only on the videos that tour the client.

questions.question: Should you enable high priority notifications or dismiss the prompt by tapping 'No thanks'?
questions.why: The inbox displays a banner offering to 'Try notifications for only your high priority emails' with options to 'Turn on' or say 'No thanks', which must be navigated or ignored to continue.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to opt into or permanently dismiss a system-level notification preference for their inbox.

questions.question: Which email app should I select from the share sheet?
questions.why: The Android share sheet displays multiple options like 'Gmail' and 'Email', requiring a choice of which specific client to use for composing the message.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide which specific email client and associated account is used to send the attachment.

questions.question: Which app do you open to access your email?
questions.why: The home screen displays multiple applications, so you must select the specific mail client you want to use to send the message.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to choose which specific email client or account is used to send the message.

questions.question: Which application should you open to access your email?
questions.why: The screen displays a desktop with multiple icons, requiring you to identify the correct web browser to begin the task.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the ability to choose your preferred web browser or specific user profile for sending the email.

questions.question: Which email provider should I use to send this message?
questions.why: The browser address bar requires a specific URL to load the correct email platform, such as Gmail or Yahoo.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means you lose control over which specific email service and associated account is used as the sender.

questions.question: How should you enter your sign-in credentials?
questions.why: The sign-in screen requires an email and password, which can be typed manually or autofilled using a password manager.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether to securely autofill your credentials using a specific password manager or type them manually.

questions.question: Which email account are you currently sending from?
questions.why: Opening the profile pop-up reveals the active email address, '[email]', ensuring the message is sent from the correct account.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to verify or switch their sender identity before composing the message.

questions.question: Do you need to verify your current email address before composing?
questions.why: Checking the profile pop-up confirms the exact email address and storage status you are currently using.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to confirm you are sending the email from the correct account.

children.label: Open a compose surface
children.note: 2.1 for a new message. 2.2 and 2.3 instead when the message answers one that arrived, entered from 8.1 - and that choice sets what 3 has left to do: reply-all arrives with To and Cc filled, forward arrives with To empty and quoted history attached. 2.4 after the draft exists. 2.5 where the compose surface is a panel that can be resized. 2.6 before typing, on the two keepers that tour the surface first.

questions.question: Do you need to click the trash can icon to discard a restored draft before starting your new email?
questions.why: The screen shows the user clicking the 'Discard draft' trash can icon before clicking 'Compose' again, which is necessary to clear the stale state if the mail client automatically restores a previous, unfinished message.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to ensure they are starting with a clean slate, risking the agent accidentally appending the new message to an old, irrelevant draft.

questions.question: How do you forward this message to someone else?
questions.why: Clicking the 'Forward' link below the thread automatically populates a new compose window with the original message and a 'Fwd:' subject line.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether to forward the existing thread or summarize the information in a brand new email.

questions.question: Should you change the response type to Reply, Reply All, or Forward?
questions.why: The screen shows a dropdown menu that lets you switch the current draft between a direct reply, a reply to all, or a forward.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to manually control exactly which participants from the original email thread will receive your message.

children.label: Set the recipients
children.note: 3.1 in nearly every keeper - typing resolved by a suggestion is close to universal here. 3.2 where the address is not in the list. 3.3 to reach the copy fields, then 3.4 and 3.5 where the message needs them. 3.6 replaces all of it on a bulk send, and rules 3.3 to 3.5 out. 3.7 whenever a chip is wrong. 3.8 before trusting a group. reply-all routes arrive with this goal already done (DFXu).

questions.question: Did the email client display a visual warning or color change indicating that the recipient is outside your organization?
questions.why: Many corporate email clients visually flag external addresses (e.g., with a yellow banner or red text) to prevent accidental data leaks, a cue that must be explicitly read if not looking at the screen.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the immediate visual alert that they are about to send potentially sensitive information to an external contact.

questions.question: Should you send this generic draft or use a different method to personalize the greeting for each recipient?
questions.why: The screen shows a single draft addressed to multiple recipients with a generic 'Hey' greeting, which prevents addressing each person by their actual name.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the personal touch of addressing each recipient by name, which makes the mass invitation feel less genuine.

questions.question: Which email address should you select as the recipient?
questions.why: The screen displays a list of multiple available email accounts, so you must select the correct one to ensure the message reaches the intended person.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means the agent might select the wrong recipient from the list, potentially sending your message to an unintended contact.

questions.question: Which specific email address do you select from the autocomplete dropdown?
questions.why: The screen shows multiple contact suggestions as you type the recipient's name, meaning you must click the correct one to proceed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the personal oversight of ensuring your message isn't accidentally routed to a similarly named but incorrect contact.

questions.question: What exact email address are you entering in the 'To' field?
questions.why: Entering the precise email address in the 'To' field ensures the message reaches the correct person instead of bouncing or going to a stranger.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to personally verify that the recipient's address is typed perfectly to avoid sending the message to the wrong person.

questions.question: Who are you sending this email to, and what are the constraints for entering their address?
questions.why: The email address must be typed perfectly without any spaces or errors, otherwise the message will fail to reach the intended recipient.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to manually verify the exact spelling and formatting of the recipient's address to ensure successful delivery.

questions.question: Who are you forwarding this email to?
questions.why: The 'To' field is empty with a blinking cursor above the forwarded content, meaning a new recipient must be specified to route the message.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide exactly which new recipient needs to receive this forwarded information.

questions.question: Does the email client flag the recipient's address in red to indicate it is improperly formatted or invalid?
questions.why: If an email address is missing an '@' symbol or a valid domain, the client usually flags it immediately with a visual error, preventing a failed send later.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to catch and correct a structural typo in the email address before attempting to send the message.

questions.question: How do you ensure recipients cannot see each other's email addresses?
questions.why: Revealing the Bcc field through the Options tab is necessary to keep the email addresses of all recipients private.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the peace of mind of personally verifying that your contacts' sensitive email addresses are properly hidden from one another.

questions.question: Who should you add as a Cc recipient?
questions.why: The dropdown suggests contacts like 'Woggle Spy Lucinda' based on your typing, requiring you to select the correct person to keep in the loop.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the ability to decide exactly who needs visibility into the conversation without being the primary recipient.

questions.question: Does the Cc field accurately reflect all original recipients, including those hidden behind the '+1' indicator?
questions.why: Confirming that the visible names and the '+1' indicator match the three original Cc recipients ensures no one is accidentally dropped from the thread.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the assurance that all necessary stakeholders are kept in the loop on the communication.

questions.question: Who should you blind carbon copy on this email?
questions.why: The screen shows an autocomplete dropdown with multiple contacts like Woggle Spy Cynthia and Woggle Spy Cuthbert for the Bcc field, requiring a choice of who should secretly receive the message.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means the agent might blind copy the wrong contact, potentially failing to keep the right person confidentially informed.

children.label: Build a bulk recipient list
children.note: 3.6.2 first - the feature has to be switched on before anything else changes. then 3.6.1, and one of 3.6.3 or the pair 3.6.4 and 3.6.5. 3.6.6 is read after the fact in this keeper, not before.

questions.question: Should you use the mail merge option to add recipients from a spreadsheet?
questions.why: Clicking the mail merge icon revealed a dropdown to add recipients from a spreadsheet, which fundamentally changes how the email is addressed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to decide whether to automate addressing a mass email using a spreadsheet or to enter recipients manually.

questions.question: Do you want to enable mail merge to send personalized, individual copies to your recipients?
questions.why: The screen displayed a mail merge menu and a banner explaining that this feature lets you personalize messages with tags and sends a separate copy to each recipient.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to choose whether to send a standard group email or utilize mail merge for personalized, individual messages.

questions.question: Which contacts do you want to include in this mail merge?
questions.why: The 'Select contacts' modal offers individual selection or a 'Select All' option for the three available contacts.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to hand-pick exactly which of your contacts should receive the message.

questions.question: Which spreadsheet contains the recipient data?
questions.why: The screen showed a 'Link a spreadsheet for recipient info' dialog displaying recent files like 'School Fees', requiring a choice of data source.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses control over which contact list is used, risking sending the email to the wrong group of people.

questions.question: Which columns from the spreadsheet will you use to personalize the email?
questions.why: Reviewing the 'School Fees' sheet ensures you know exactly which fields, like 'Amount Due' and 'Account Number', are available to insert into the message.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the opportunity to manually verify that the data source contains all the necessary and correct fields before generating the emails.

questions.question: Do you need to verify your account's daily send limits before adding a large number of recipients?
questions.why: Gmail restricts standard accounts to 500 outgoing messages and mail merge to 1,500 recipients per day, meaning exceeding these limits will block your emails from sending.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the awareness of your account's specific sending thresholds, which could result in a blocked campaign if the agent blindly exceeds the limit.

questions.question: Are you aware of the Cc, Bcc, and scheduling limitations when using a spreadsheet to add recipients?
questions.why: The help page explicitly states that using a spreadsheet for mail merge prevents you from adding Cc or Bcc recipients and disables features like schedule send and confidential mode.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to weigh whether the convenience of a spreadsheet outweighs the need to copy other recipients or schedule the email.

questions.question: Do you need to use features like schedule send or confidential mode that aren't supported by mail merge?
questions.why: The expanded limitations section explicitly states that mail merge cannot be used with replies, forwards, scheduled sends, or confidential mode.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the awareness of specific feature incompatibilities that might prevent your email from being sent exactly as you intended.

questions.question: Is the intended contact group available to select in the dropdown?
questions.why: Seeing the 'Test Group' entry with its member count in the autocomplete dropdown confirms the mail client recognizes your pre-made distribution list.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you cannot visually verify the group's member count to ensure the exact right list of people will receive your message.

questions.question: How do you verify who is included in a contact group?
questions.why: Checking the details pane for 'Test Group' ensures you know exactly which email addresses, like Christian and Dad, will receive the message.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the peace of mind of manually reviewing and confirming the exact individuals included in a group alias before the email goes out.

children.label: Write the message
children.note: 4.1 then 4.2 - HnFK does both before the recipient. 4.3 where the client suggests text mid-typing. 4.4 only where the content comes from another application. 4.5 on a forward, before the quoted history travels with it. 4.6 once per field the spreadsheet supplies. 4.7 is opened in three keepers and applied in one.

questions.question: What date, time, and duration should you set for the scheduled meeting?
questions.why: The 'Schedule Meeting' window requires you to configure the 'Topic', 'Start' date and time, and 'Duration' to generate the correct invitation details.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the control to pick a specific date and time that perfectly aligns with your unwritten scheduling preferences.

questions.question: Should I use your Personal Meeting ID or generate one automatically, and do you want to require a password?
questions.why: The screen shows options to either generate a meeting ID automatically or use a Personal Meeting ID, along with a checkbox to require a meeting password.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to balance convenience and security for their specific meeting participants.

questions.question: Should I enable video for the host and participants?
questions.why: The screen showed radio buttons to toggle video on or off for the host and participants, which sets the default camera behavior for the integrated meeting.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to dictate the meeting's visual engagement and privacy boundaries based on their relationship with the attendees.

questions.question: Which audio options do you want to allow for the meeting?
questions.why: The screen displayed radio buttons to choose between Telephone, Computer Audio, or both for the meeting details being added to the email.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The delegator loses the ability to specify how recipients are allowed to dial into or connect to the meeting.

questions.question: Which calendar system should you select for scheduling?
questions.why: The screen presents radio buttons for Outlook, Google Calendar, and Other Calendars, requiring a choice for the scheduling integration.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to ensure the scheduling tool aligns with their preferred personal or corporate calendar ecosystem.

questions.question: Do you want to enable any advanced meeting settings, such as allowing participants to join before the host?
questions.why: The screen showed a collapsed 'Advanced Options' menu containing specific settings for waiting rooms, early joining, and automatic recording.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to control the specific entry and recording behaviors for their meeting attendees.

questions.question: What should you enter as the subject and body of the email?
questions.why: The screen displays empty 'Subject' and 'Compose email' fields that require the actual content of your message.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose control over the exact wording, tone, and personal touch of the message sent on your behalf.

questions.question: Do you need to edit or delete the auto-inserted email signature for this specific message?
questions.why: Mail clients often automatically append a default signature to the bottom of the message body, which you might want to remove for casual replies or edit to hide a phone number.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to tailor their sign-off and control what personal contact information is shared in the specific context of this email.

questions.question: Should you mark the message with 'High Importance' or flag it for 'Follow Up'?
questions.why: The Outlook message ribbon contains explicit buttons for 'High Importance' and 'Follow Up' that alter how the email is presented and tracked.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to explicitly signal the urgency of the message to the recipient or set a reminder for themselves.

questions.question: Is your default email signature correctly positioned at the bottom of the draft without being accidentally deleted or duplicated?
questions.why: Automated agents or careless pasting can easily overwrite the pre-filled default signature or paste a second one, making the email look unprofessional.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the assurance that their standard professional sign-off and contact information are intact and properly formatted.

questions.question: What should you write in the subject line to grab the recipient's attention?
questions.why: A relevant and compelling subject line ensures the recipient prioritizes the email in a crowded inbox.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally gauge the recipient's priorities and craft a subject line tailored to catch their specific attention.

questions.question: What should you enter as the subject of the email?
questions.why: The screen shows an empty 'Subject:' field that requires a concise summary of the email's purpose.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to craft a specific subject line that sets the right tone and context for your recipient.

questions.question: What do you want to write in the message body?
questions.why: The 'Compose email' field is where the actual content and details of your message must be entered.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose control over the exact wording, tone, and specific details communicated to the recipient.

questions.question: Is the auto-filled recipient correct, and what should you type in your reply before sending?
questions.why: The compose interface automatically populates the 'To:' field with the original sender's address and quotes their message, requiring you to confirm the recipient and add your own text.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the opportunity to verify exactly who the reply is going to and to craft the specific wording of your response.

questions.question: Should you interact with the Smart Compose tooltip or ignore it and type your message manually?
questions.why: The screen displays a Smart Compose tooltip offering writing suggestions that can be acknowledged, disabled, or simply ignored while drafting.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the choice of whether to utilize, dismiss, or permanently disable the AI writing suggestions for your account.

questions.question: Do you want to use the 'Help me write' AI options to formalize, elaborate, or shorten your draft?
questions.why: The compose window displays a 'Help me write' menu with options like 'Formalize', 'Elaborate', and 'Shorten' that can automatically rewrite the text you entered.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide whether to rely on AI to adjust the tone and length of their message or to send their own exact words.

questions.question: Should you include instructions on how to open the attached zip file?
questions.why: The screen showed the user copying tutorial links from a Google Doc into the email body to ensure the recipient can successfully access the zipped attachment.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to proactively anticipate the recipient's technical limitations and provide helpful context alongside your attachments.

questions.question: How do you retrieve the meeting invitation details?
questions.why: The 'Zoom - Schedule Meeting' dialog offers options to open with a default calendar or copy to the clipboard.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to review the meeting details before they are copied and sent.

questions.question: Should you keep or delete the forwarded email history below your new message?
questions.why: The screen shows the previous email thread appended below the new message, which might clutter the email or include unnecessary context.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to curate the email's context and ensure the recipient only sees the relevant information you intended to share.

questions.question: Which merge tag do you want to use for the greeting?
questions.why: The screen shows a menu of mail merge tags like '@ firstname' and '@ lastname', which determines how the recipient's name will be formatted in the automated greeting.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The delegator loses control over the tone of the email by not being able to choose between a casual first name or a more formal full name greeting.

questions.question: Which merge tag do you select to replace the date placeholder?
questions.why: Typing the '@' symbol brings up the mail merge tags dropdown, requiring you to choose the exact variable that will correctly populate the recipient's payment deadline.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to ensure the correct dynamic data tag is used for sensitive information like a payment due date.

questions.question: Which mail merge tags do you select for the account number and amount due?
questions.why: The draft includes placeholders for billing details, requiring you to select the correct dynamic fields from the mail merge menu to populate them accurately.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the ability to verify that the correct data fields are mapped to the sensitive billing information in your email template.

questions.question: Are all the purple placeholder tags correctly positioned in your draft?
questions.why: Verifying the purple highlight tags like '@firstname' and '@amountdue' ensures the mail merge will populate the correct data for each recipient before you click Continue.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally verify that sensitive merge fields like account numbers and amounts due are placed in the correct context within the message.

questions.question: Does the pasted text contain broken formatting or unreadable background colors that need to be cleared?
questions.why: Pasting content from external documents or websites often imports incompatible HTML formatting, making the email look broken or unprofessional.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The ability to notice and strip out corrupted rich-text formatting before the recipient sees a garbled message.

children.label: Attach a file
children.note: 5.1 opens the source list, and which sources exist is the client's decision, not the user's. then 5.2, or 5.3 where the file is dragged in instead, or 5.5 where it lives in cloud storage. 5.4 fires when the client refuses what was picked, and returns into 5.2 or 5.5 once the file is ready. 5.6 where the upload has to finish before anything else. three keepers open 5.1 and attach nothing at all.

questions.question: Do you need to attach any files or Drive links to this email?
questions.why: The compose toolbar displays icons for attaching local files or inserting from Google Drive, prompting a choice about including supplementary documents.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the ability to judge whether additional context or specific documents should accompany your message.

questions.question: Do you want to attach the file directly, or share it by generating a link?
questions.why: The file's context menu offers options like 'Get link' and 'Download', meaning you must choose whether to send a cloud link or a physical attachment.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide the file sharing method, which affects whether the recipient needs specific cloud permissions to view the document.

questions.question: Which source should you select from the Attach File dropdown?
questions.why: The dropdown offers recent items, web locations, and the local PC, so you must specify where the intended file is currently stored.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide exactly which storage location to pull the attachment from, risking the selection of an incorrect or outdated version of the file.

questions.question: Which file do you select to attach to the email?
questions.why: Choosing the correct file from the Downloads folder ensures the intended image, such as 'Cool Guy.jpg', is attached to the email.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to manually browse your folders and visually verify you are attaching the exact file you intended.

questions.question: Which file do you select from the opened folder to attach?
questions.why: The file picker displays various files like 'man-152231_1280.png' and 'Spreadsheet.xlsx', requiring you to choose the exact item to include.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose control over exactly which specific file from your local folder is shared with the recipient.

questions.question: Which folder contains the image you want to attach?
questions.why: The file manager displays multiple image directories like Camera, Downloads, and Canva, so you must know exactly where the intended attachment is saved.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means losing the ability to visually browse your personal folders to find the exact image you intended to share.

questions.question: Which files do you want to attach from this folder?
questions.why: The file explorer shows several audio and document files like 'Script.docx' and 'Google Maps Spanish.m4a', so the exact files to include must be specified.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to browse the folder's contents and manually select the specific combination of files to share.

questions.question: Have I selected the correct files, and how do I confirm the selection?
questions.why: The top bar explicitly shows '3 selected', requiring a tap on the 'Select' button to finalize adding them to the email.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally verify that the correct documents or images are being attached before they are added to the draft.

questions.question: Where do you navigate to find the file you want to attach?
questions.why: Navigating directly to the specific drive avoids accidentally selecting the wrong file from the recent files list, which displayed sensitive data.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the peace of mind that the agent won't accidentally select and attach a sensitive file from the recent files list.

questions.question: Should you grant the app permission to access all your photos?
questions.why: The system dialog requires you to choose whether to give the app access to all your photos, select specific ones, or deny access entirely.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to protect your privacy by restricting the app's access to only specific photos rather than your entire library.

questions.question: Which file are you dragging into the compose window to attach?
questions.why: The screen shows a 'Drop files here' overlay in Gmail as a file from the Downloads folder is dragged over it, which dictates exactly what attachment the recipient will receive.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to manually verify the specific file being dragged from your local directory before it is attached to the message.

questions.question: Do you want to resize the inline image?
questions.why: The screen shows options like 'Small' and 'Best fit' to control how the inline image appears within the email body.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to visually verify the image's layout and choose the best fit for the recipient's reading experience.

children.label: Prepare the file elsewhere
children.note: 5.4.1 names what stopped it. then whichever of 5.4.2 to 5.4.5 the block calls for: a folder gets compressed, an oversized file gets uploaded, a cloud file gets its sharing set, a cloud file that has to travel as bytes gets downloaded first. 5.4.6 where the client is not connected to the storage service at all. 5.4.3 after any compression. then back into 5.2 or 5.5 - UehN is the one keeper that never gets back.

questions.question: Can you attach an entire folder directly to the email?
questions.why: Selecting a folder and clicking 'Open' in the file browser merely opens it to reveal contents like 'road-259815_1280.jpg' rather than attaching the folder itself.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the awareness that folders cannot be attached directly and must either be zipped or have their individual files selected.

questions.question: Did the email client reject the attachment and display a security warning about a restricted file type?
questions.why: Mail clients actively block certain file extensions (like .exe, .bat, or scripts) for security, requiring the user to find an alternative sharing method like a cloud link.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the awareness that their specific file type is prohibited and will fail to attach, requiring a change in delivery strategy.

questions.question: Do you want to use Mail Drop to send this oversized attachment?
questions.why: The attachment is 56.3 MB, which exceeds the 52.4 MB limit, prompting Apple Mail to offer iCloud delivery.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to choose whether your file is temporarily hosted on iCloud or sent directly through your email provider.

questions.question: Which folder needs to be compressed?
questions.why: The screen shows a File Explorer window with 'Folder To Be Emailed', which must be selected and compressed before it can be attached.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to specify exactly which folder should be prepared and attached to the email.

questions.question: Is the option to compress the folder available in this context menu?
questions.why: The context menu for the Zoom folder lacks a compress or zip option, which is necessary because most email clients require folders to be zipped before attaching.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide whether to troubleshoot the missing compression tool or simply abandon this folder and attach a different one.

questions.question: What do you do when you get a 'Compressed (zipped) Folders Error' stating the folder is empty?
questions.why: The screen shows an error dialog because the system cannot zip an empty directory, halting your attempt to prepare the attachment.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to realize they forgot to put their intended files into the folder before trying to attach it to the email.

questions.question: Are these the correct files to compress and attach?
questions.why: The screen showed the contents of 'Folder To Be Emailed', allowing verification of the files before zipping them for the email.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the visual confirmation that all intended files are present in the folder before it gets compressed and sent.

questions.question: Did you verify the folder successfully compressed into a .zip file?
questions.why: Confirming the completion notification and locating the new .zip file in the directory ensures the folder is actually ready to be attached.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the visual reassurance of seeing the newly created .zip file appear in your directory before it gets attached.

questions.question: Do you want to rename the newly created ZIP file?
questions.why: The text 'Folder To Be Emailed' is highlighted in an editable text box, giving you the immediate option to customize the file name before attaching it.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to apply a specific or more professional naming convention to the attachment that the recipient will see.

questions.question: Do you confirm the browser's security warning to upload the entire folder?
questions.why: The browser explicitly asks if you trust the site before allowing the upload of all 10 files from the selected folder.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally assess the security warning and explicitly grant the site access to your local files.

questions.question: Is the file you want to attach already uploaded to your Google Drive?
questions.why: The Google Drive file picker displayed 'No files found,' indicating that the file must be uploaded to Drive first before it can be attached.
